options.B: Direct absorption of dietary vitamin D through pores
options.C: Secretion of active vitamin D via sweat glands
options.D: Enzymatic breakdown of subcutaneous fat deposits

explanation: Ultraviolet B rays convert cholesterol precursors in the skin into cholecalciferol, which is later processed into active vitamin D by the liver and kidneys. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h1)

question: When should a woman with a history of gestational diabetes undergo a postpartum glucose tolerance test to reclassify her status?

options.A: At 6 weeks postpartum
options.B: Only during her subsequent pregnancy
options.C: Within 24 hours after delivery
options.D: At 6 months postpartum

explanation: The standard clinical guideline is to perform a 75-gram OGTT around 6 weeks postpartum to confirm whether gestational glucose intolerance has resolved or progressed to overt diabetes. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h8)

question: What is a primary responsibility of the community health nurse in managing chronic hypertension?

options.A: Diagnosing rare endocrine disorders without physician consultation
options.B: Providing culturally tailored education on lifestyle modification and medication adherence
options.C: Manufacturing generic antihypertensive drugs for distribution in local clinics
options.D: Performing complex surgical procedures to repair damaged renal arteries

explanation: Community nurses bridge the gap by teaching patients in understandable language how to manage their condition daily. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T2#GNS313_U3_T2_h9)

question: Who must standard precautions be applied to in the clinical environment?

options.A: Only patients with confirmed viral hemorrhagic fevers
options.B: Individuals showing visible symptoms of respiratory distress
options.C: All patients regardless of their infection status
options.D: Patients admitted specifically to the intensive care unit

explanation: Standard precautions assume that every patient's blood and body fluids are potentially infectious, making them universal for all care. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h3)

question: What is the approximate minimum level of medication adherence generally required to maintain viral suppression and prevent resistance?

options.A: At least 85%
options.B: At least 50%
options.C: At least 95%
options.D: At least 70%

explanation: Antiretroviral therapy requires near-perfect adherence—typically defined as taking at least 95% of doses on schedule—to prevent the virus from mutating and developing resistance. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T4#GNS216_U6_T4_h7)

question: Which action is most appropriate during post-test counseling for a client with a negative HIV result?

options.A: Reporting the negative test to local public health registries
options.B: Prescribing a standard regimen of antiretroviral drugs
options.C: Isolating the client to prevent future exposure risks
options.D: Providing targeted risk-reduction education and prevention strategies

explanation: A negative result serves as an educational opportunity to discuss prevention methods and maintain a safe status. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T10#GNS216_U6_T10_h5)

question: How is an Adverse Event Following Immunization (AEFI) broadly defined?

options.A: Any untoward medical occurrence happening after vaccine administration
options.B: Permanent physical disabilities resulting exclusively from cold chain failure
options.C: Only severe allergic reactions caused by chemical preservatives
options.D: Guaranteed systemic symptoms that occur in every vaccinated infant

explanation: An AEFI encompasses any health issue arising after vaccination, requiring investigation to determine if the vaccine caused it. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T75#GNS214_U1_T75_h6)

question: What is a major physiological contributor to stress urinary incontinence in multiparous women?

options.A: Enlargement of the prostate gland near the bladder neck
options.B: Atrophy of the renal cortex due to aging nephrons
options.C: Chronic hypersecretion of antidiuretic hormone by the pituitary gland
options.D: Stretching and weakening of the pelvic floor muscles during childbirth

explanation: Vaginal deliveries place intense mechanical stress on the pelvic floor, often damaging the supportive tissues around the bladder neck. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h4)

question: A nurse leader drafts an advocacy message to local councilors regarding malnourished children. Which sentence represents the best call to action?

options.A: We hope everyone can think about the hungry children in our local government area
options.B: Approve the supplementary nutrition budget line at the next council meeting on Thursday
options.C: Child malnutrition is a very serious problem that affects our entire community
options.D: Nurses should provide more nutrition counseling during weekly antenatal clinics

explanation: This option gives a specific, actionable task to the exact audience targeted by the advocacy message. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T8#GNS124_U4_T8_h4)

question: Which factor plays the largest role in determining whether body image changes during gestation are perceived positively or negatively?

options.A: A complex interplay of personal self-esteem, partner reactions, and cultural norms
options.B: The exact numerical baseline weight recorded at the very first antenatal visit
options.C: The total absence of any stretch marks or physical skin pigmentation shifts
options.D: Strict adherence to strenuous athletic training routines during early pregnancy

explanation: Body image perception is subjective, shaped heavily by personal psychology, societal standards of beauty, and validation from loved ones. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T004#GNS226_U2_T004_h4)

question: Which characteristic is essential for a delivery to be officially classified as a normal labour?

options.A: Elective induction of contractions
options.B: Surgical rupture of membranes early
options.C: Breech presentation with assistance
options.D: Spontaneous vertex presentation

explanation: A normal labour requires the fetus to present head-first by the vertex spontaneously without complex surgical maneuvers. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T002#GNS226_U3_T002_h1)
